facts.statement: The study examined how the brain represents language in people who speak 21 different languages.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The researchers used brain scan data from 12 languages that were already available and collected new brain scan data for 9 more languages.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The goal was to see if computer models that understand multiple languages could predict how the brain's language areas react to words.
facts.subject: computational

facts.statement: The computer models were able to accurately predict brain activity for each individual language tested.
facts.subject: computational

facts.statement: Models trained on some languages could predict brain activity for other languages they had never seen before.
facts.subject: computational

facts.statement: This ability to predict brain activity for new languages worked across different language groups, types of words, and ways the words were presented.
facts.subject: computational

facts.statement: The results suggest that the brain uses a common system to process meaning across all human languages.
facts.subject: humans
